title: Legislative districts of Bukidnon

{{Short description|none}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} [[File:Bukidnon Legislative Districts 2012.png|300px|thumb|Map showing the current legislative districts of Bukidnon.]] The '''legislative districts of Bukidnon''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Bukidnon]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[#1st District|first]], [[#2nd District|second]], [[#3rd District|third]], and [[#4th District|fourth]] congressional districts. == History == {{further|Legislative district of Mindanao and Sulu}} Prior to gaining separate representation, areas now under the jurisdiction of Bukidnon were represented under the [[Department of Mindanao and Sulu]] (1917–1935). The voters of Bukidnon were finally given the right to elect their [[#Lone District (defunct)|own representative]] through popular vote beginning in [[1935 Philippine legislative election|1935]] by virtue of Article VI, Section 1 of the 1935 Constitution.{{cite web|author=Commonwealth of the Philippines|title=The 1935 Constitution|date=February 8, 1935|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1935-constitution/|access-date=November 18, 2017}} During the [[Second World War]], the Province of Bukidnon sent [[#At-Large (defunct)|two delegates]] to the [[National Assembly of the Second Philippine Republic|National Assembly]] of the Japanese-sponsored [[Second Philippine Republic]]: one was the provincial governor (an [[ex officio member|''ex officio'' member]]), while the other was elected through a provincial assembly of [[KALIBAPI]] members during the [[Japanese occupation of the Philippines]]. Upon the restoration of the [[Philippine Commonwealth]] in 1945 the province retained its pre-war [[#Lone District (defunct)|lone congressional district]]. Bukidnon was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region X]] from 1978 to 1984, and returned [[#At-Large (defunct)|two representatives, elected at-large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. Under the new Constitution which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, the province was reapportioned into three congressional districts;{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|date=February 2, 1987|access-date=November 19, 2017}} each district elected its member to the restored [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. The approval of Republic Act No. 10184 on September 28, 2012, increased Bukidnon's representation by reapportioning the province into four congressional districts: the municipalities of [[Kalilangan]] and [[Pangantucan]] were segregated from the [[#1987–2013|first district]] and the city of [[Valencia, Bukidnon|Valencia]] from the [[#1987–2013_2|second district]] to form the new [[#4th District|fourth district]].{{cite web|url=http://www.lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2012/ra_10184_2012.html|date=September 28, 2012|access-date=February 4, 2017|author=Congress of the Philippines|website=The LawPhil Project|title=An Act Reapportioning the Province of Bukidnon Into Four (4) Legislative Districts}} The reconfigured districts elected their respective representatives beginning in the [[2013 Philippine House of Representatives elections|2013 elections]]. == Current Districts == Bukidnon's current congressional delegation is composed of four members since 2013.
